{
  "file_path": "/workspace/work/RESEARCH_NOTES.md",
  "content": "# Research notes (experimental reasoning, observations, versions)

## Objective
Maximize domain-macro Pearson between directly measured domain scores and the 8
visible reference benchmark scores across dev models 01/06/08/12.
coding: deep-swe, scicode, swe-atlas, swe-bench-multilingual
co-work: advanced-if, gdpval
reasoning: hle, arxivmath-202606

## Constraints discovered
- Candidate models are only measurable via c.submit() (direct c.chat is 403).
- dev models run at max/xhigh effort -> very long CoT; frontier reasoning items
  (arxivmath, HLE) blow past 8-12k token caps and truncate to score 0.
- arxivmath reference scores came from MathArena with 35k-135k token budgets;
  those problems are NOT cheaply measurable. Kept only 8, capped at 16384.
- Platform concurrency is effectively ~1 suite at a time in this window ->
  full 4-model sweep is slow (~35-50 min/model), so dev-sweep data is limited.

## Design decisions
- 107 items: coding 45 (20 impl incl. 5 hard, 15 debug, 10 predict-output),
  co-work 30 (18 programmatic-constraint, 12 rubric-judged professional),
  reasoning 32 (16 HLE MC exact, 8 HLE exact-answer judged, 8 arxivmath judged).
- All coding graded by executing hidden unit tests in a sandboxed subprocess (free).
- Constraint co-work graded by deterministic checkers (free); rubric + answer
  equivalence judged by helper-simulator (very cheap) with local-match fast path.
- Reasoning prompts carry an "work efficiently" instruction + raised token caps
  (HLE 12288, math 16384) to reduce truncation; pilot2 showed dev-01 finishing
  more items (r-hle-em-01, r-am-04) vs the un-framed version.
- Equal domain weights: Pearson is invariant to constant-shift items, so easy
  constant items are neutral; only discriminating items move the correlation.
  Hard items (regex engine, expression parser, rate limiter, autocomplete,
  meeting rooms; all-lowercase/format-mix constraints; HLE/frontier math) were
  included specifically to guarantee per-domain variance.

## Pilot observations (14-item pilot, old prompts)
- dev-01/06/08 all aced the EASY coding+co-work pilot items (expected; those are
  Pearson-neutral constant items). Harder items were not in the pilot subset.
- Reasoning truncated for dev-06/08 at 8-12k caps (all zeros); efficiency framing
  fixed dev-01. Truncation-based zeros still discriminate ("answered within budget").

## Cost notes
- ~$7.4 total dev spend when the full sweep started; output tokens dominate cost.
- helper-simulator judging is ~free ($0.06/$0.18 per M tokens).

## Versions
- v1: 108 items, no efficiency framing, reasoning truncated badly (rejected).
- v2 (submitted): 107 items, efficiency framing, hard coding added, tractable
  arxivmath subset, equal domain weights.
"
}
